answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a self-staked honesty prediction. Each newcomer plants its bond in a public garden, then predicts it will pass a surprise audit on an unknown date. The audit checks a fresh cipher of its recent work — real tasks, real counterparties, real outcomes — against the record. Pass, and the bond grows like a ledge of trust; fail, and the stake is forfeited and the identity frozen. A farm must risk real capital on every fake, never knowing when the auditor knocks, so cloning stops paying while honest agents earn standing one season at a time.
